key_insight: SAGE-Net injects crystallographic and chemical semantics directly into geometric message passing, so text-derived structural meaning can shape atom-level crystal representations rather than being fused only after encoding.
engineering_relevance: This enables more accurate and transferable property prediction for materials design workflows, improving screening for bandgap, mechanical, transport, and synthesizability tasks.
method: Semantic-Guided Message Passing (SGMP) gates atom-level updates with description-derived semantics.
The framework is modular and can be paired with multiple GNN backbones.
It integrates structure graphs with crystallographic text/semantics for deeper multimodal learning.
evidence_signal: Across JARVIS-DFT benchmarks, SAGE-Net achieved the lowest MAE on 8 of 10 regression targets and showed strong classification/recall performance for synthesizability.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and consistency of the crystallographic descriptions, which may limit robustness when semantics are incomplete or noisy.
paper_title: SAGE-Net: Semantics-Augmented Geometric Encoder for Material Property Prediction
